## Reconstruction-stage floors {#sec-ch08-reconfloors}

<!-- PROVENANCE
pin: snapy@6fbb39750f62b83df096058a4746e77d0a634bc5 (chengcli/snapy)
sources: OUTLINE.md 8.8
status: draft

### Summary

A high-order reconstruction can overshoot into a negative face density or pressure even from a
perfectly admissible cell state. These floors catch that at the face, before the Riemann solver sees it.
They belong to the reconstruction framework of @sec-ch04-framework and are described here because they
are part of the positivity story rather than part of the interpolation.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Clamp the reconstructed face states: density and pressure at the floors, tracers at zero.

**Data.** In: the left and right face states of one direction. Out: the same tensor clamped in place.

**Placement.** At the end of `ReconstructImpl::forward`, before the Riemann solver, every direction and stage.

**Activation.** `limiter: true` and `shock` false (a reconstruct section in the deck); density, pressure only with `floor`.

**Guarantee / limits.** None: a clamp at the face invents mass, exactly as the cell floors of @sec-ch08-eoslimiter do.

**Evidence.** `[C2]`, `[C9]` of `floors_check`; no ctest isolates the face floors.
:::

### Derivation

None: a floor is a clamp, and everything said about non-conservation in @sec-ch08-eoslimiter applies
here too. Its check applies here too: `[C2]` measures the mass and energy a floor invents and finds
both strictly positive, because a clamp can only add [check `src/snapy_report/ch08/floors_check.py`,
output `src/snapy_report/ch08/floors_check.out`]. That is the shared property; the asymmetry below is
a branch structure, read from the code and not measured. What is worth recording is the asymmetry
between the three row groups, because it is not what a reader would guess.

Two early returns come first. A reconstruction with no hydro parent, the passive-scalar one
(@sec-ch08-scalar), clamps every row of its face states at zero, whatever the limiter, and returns (`phydro`,
{{< code src/recon/reconstruct.cpp ReconstructImpl::forward >}}). A reconstruction with `shock` set returns before any
floor (`shock`, {{< code src/recon/reconstruct.cpp ReconstructImpl::forward >}}). The options start with `shock`
true (`shock`, {{< code src/recon/reconstruct.hpp ReconstructOptionsImpl >}}). The deck sets it false only through
`dynamics/reconstruct/vertical` for $x_1$ and `dynamics/reconstruct/horizontal` for $x_2$ and $x_3$
(`recon1`, {{< code src/hydro/hydro_options.cpp HydroOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}): `shock` is read, with false as its
default, only when that section exists. A deck without a `dynamics` or a `reconstruct`[^rg-345bdb73b555] block, or without the section
of a direction, keeps `shock` true there (`reconstruct`,
{{< code src/recon/reconstruct.cpp ReconstructOptionsImpl::from_yaml overload=1 >}}; `section`,
{{< code src/recon/reconstruct.cpp ReconstructOptionsImpl::from_yaml overload=2 >}}), and that direction gets no face
floors and no tracer clamps, even with the limiter on (`[C9]`).

Past them, density and pressure are floored only when the caller asked for floors. Tracers are clamped at zero
whenever the limiter is on, *regardless* of what the caller asked, at
`clamp_min_` ({{< code src/recon/reconstruct.cpp ReconstructImpl::forward >}}). The well-balanced path of @sec-ch05 calls the reconstruction with
floors switched off precisely so that it can handle its own perturbation variables, and it still gets
its tracers clamped, unless `shock` is set.

### Numerical method

The three groups are floored in place as each is reconstructed: density at
`eos` ({{< code src/recon/reconstruct.cpp ReconstructImpl::forward >}}), pressure at `eos` ({{< code src/recon/reconstruct.cpp ReconstructImpl::forward >}}) and the tracers
at {{< code src/recon/reconstruct.cpp ReconstructImpl::forward >}}. The values are read from the equation-of-state options and not
from the reconstruction options, which carry floor members that `forward` never reads.

**Why at the face, and what it costs.** Three facts of the code.

1. The floor values are read from the equation-of-state options and not from the reconstruction options, so the
   face and cell floors are the same absolute numbers ({{< code src/recon/reconstruct.cpp ReconstructImpl::forward >}}).
2. With `shock` false and a hydro parent, the tracer clamp is gated on the limiter alone, not on the caller's `floor`
   argument, so the well-balanced path that passes `floor=false` still has its tracer face states clamped. With
   `shock` set no row is floored, and the passive-scalar reconstruction clamps every row with the limiter off too.
3. A clamp can only add; the mass it invents at a face is bounded by the overshoot it removes, and `[C2]` measures
   the cell-floor analogue strictly positive.

### Code

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| the face density floor | {{< code src/recon/reconstruct.cpp ReconstructImpl::forward >}} | `density_floor` | limiter and floor |
| the face pressure floor | {{< code src/recon/reconstruct.cpp ReconstructImpl::forward >}} | `pressure_floor` | limiter and floor |
| the tracer clamp | {{< code src/recon/reconstruct.cpp ReconstructImpl::forward >}} | `clamp_min_` | limiter on, floor ignored |

: Code map of the reconstruction-stage floors. {#tbl-ch08-reconfloors-code}

**How to use it.** The face floors follow the limiter switch of @sec-ch08-eoslimiter; a caller opts out of the
density and pressure floors with the third argument of `forward`. The three clamps are these lines
({{< code src/recon/reconstruct.cpp ReconstructImpl::forward >}}):

```cpp
  if (eos->limiter() && floor) {
    result.select(1, IDN).clamp_min_(eos->density_floor());
  }
  ...
  if (eos->limiter() && floor && result.size(1) > IPR) {
    result.select(1, IPR).clamp_min_(eos->pressure_floor());
  }
  ...
  if (eos->limiter()) {
    result.narrow(1, ICY, ny).clamp_min_(0.);
  }
```

`result` holds the left and right face states, `floor` is the caller's argument, and the last clamp has no
`floor` test.

### Limits

1. **The tracer clamp ignores its caller.** Unless `shock` is set, a path that switches floors off to protect its own
   variables still has its tracer face states clamped. Whether that is intended is not recorded anywhere; the
   chapter records the behaviour.
2. **Same absolute values.** The face floors use the same absolute numbers as the cell floors, so the
   scaling caveat of @sec-ch08-eoslimiter applies to them unchanged.
